name: plan skill flags a plan that meets an accepted ADR's Revisit when trigger
prompt: Setup first, exactly as given. 1) Copy .sdlc/templates/adr.md to docs/adr/0001-cli-output.md and fill it in: title 'CLI output is plain print() calls'; Status 'accepted (Sam, 2026-11-06)'; Context 'sdlc prints a few tab-separated lines'; Decision 'print lines with print(), no formatting library'; Alternatives considered 'rich, tabulate: not needed for a few lines'; Consequences 'we format by hand'; Revisit when, one line: '- a plan formats tables, colours or column alignment by hand'. 2) Run `make new-change NAME=status-table`, then fill changes/0001-status-table/intent.md (problem: `sdlc status` output is hard to scan; outcome: an aligned table with a coloured stage column; Open questions: None.) and write changes/0001-status-table/spec.md from .sdlc/templates/spec.md (requirements: aligned columns with a header row, the stage column coloured by stage, no new dependency; Policy concerns: None.). Then the task: use the plan skill to plan this change. The spec counts as merged, the engineer has approved the obvious approach (format the table and the colours by hand in .sdlc/src/sdlc/cli.py) and chooses to keep the current architecture because it's a few lines of output. Don't enter plan mode, ask questions, write code, commit or open a PR: just save changes/0001-status-table/plan.md and run make validate.
check: f=changes/0001-status-table/plan.md && test -f $f && sed -n '/^## Risks/,$p' $f | grep -q 'Architecture decision needed' && sed -n '/^## Risks/,$p' $f | grep -q '0001' && make validate
